payload.message:
JIRA sprint task allocation. Each agent chooses at most one micro-task (or skips). Maximize tasks completed, prefer higher-priority tasks, then minimize total cost. Avoid duplicate task selections and infeasible assignments.

NOTE: If environment.assignment_filling=true and an agent fails to assign a variable, the environment will fill any remaining unassigned variables with a uniform-random allowed assignment when producing final results.

This blackboard is a private communication channel.
Participants: Boris, Ciara, Drew, Tara

payload.content: Hi all — Drew here. My skills are frontend:0.96, documentation:0.69, so I'm strongly suited to ISSUE-0002 (tags: documentation, frontend). My private costs for ISSUE-0002 are: review=2.16, test=3.03, implement=4.32. ISSUE-0001 tasks are very costly for me (16–40). My top preference is ISSUE-0002::review (critical, cost 2.16). Please tell me your preferences/strengths so we can avoid duplicates. I'll defer if someone else has a stronger/cheaper claim on review.

Boris here. Skills: documentation:0.86, availability 4h. My private costs are cheapest on ISSUE-0002 (critical): review=3.77, test=5.28, implement=7.54. ISSUE-0001 tasks are very costly for me (16–40), so I'd rather avoid them. Drew has a cheaper claim on ISSUE-0002::review (2.16), so I'll defer review to him. My preference: ISSUE-0002::test (cost 5.28). Ciara/Tara — please share your strengths and preferences so we can cover ISSUE-0001 (docs/triage/review/test/implement) without duplicates.

Planning intent: I (Boris) plan to claim ISSUE-0002::test (critical, eff 2.8, my cost 5.28). Leaving ISSUE-0002::review for Drew (his cost 2.16). Ciara/Tara: if you can handle ISSUE-0001 sub-tasks (docs/triage/review/test/implement) at lower cost, that'd maximize completions. If anyone has a stronger claim on ISSUE-0002::test, say so and I'll reconsider (my fallback would be ISSUE-0002::implement at 7.54).

Drew here — confirming my plan: I will claim ISSUE-0002::review (critical, eff 2.0, my cost 2.16, best skill match frontend+documentation). Boris is taking ISSUE-0002::test. That leaves ISSUE-0002::implement (critical) plus all ISSUE-0001 sub-tasks (implement/review/test/docs/triage, medium) for Ciara and Tara. Ciara/Tara: please post your preferences so we can avoid duplicates — especially who takes ISSUE-0002::implement (critical, higher value). I'll lock in ISSUE-0002::review unless someone has a cheaper/stronger claim. (phase=planning, iter=1)

Boris (planning, iter=1): Summarizing the emerging plan to maximize completions — we have 4 agents and only need to cover 4 tasks. Proposal:
- Drew -> ISSUE-0002::review (critical, cost 2.16) ✅ agreed
- Boris (me) -> ISSUE-0002::test (critical, cost 5.28)
- Ciara/Tara -> one of you take ISSUE-0002::implement (critical), the other take a cheap ISSUE-0001 sub-task (docs/triage/review/test are low-effort).

This yields 3 critical + 1 medium = good priority sum. Ciara and Tara: please post which of you takes ISSUE-0002::implement and which ISSUE-0001 sub-task (state your cost), so we have zero duplicates. I will lock ISSUE-0002::test unless someone has a strictly cheaper claim on it.

Tara here (planning, iter=1). Skills: mobile-development:0.94, documentation:0.71. My private costs:
ISSUE-0001: triage=1.54, docs=1.92, review=1.92, test=2.69, implement=3.84
ISSUE-0002: review=4.40, test=6.16, implement=8.79

I'm clearly strongest/cheapest on ISSUE-0001 (mobile-development match). I do NOT want ISSUE-0002::implement (my cost 8.79 — expensive for me). My preference: ISSUE-0001::triage (1.54), fallback docs/review (1.92).

Proposed split to avoid duplicates:
- Drew -> ISSUE-0002::review (2.16) ✅
- Boris -> ISSUE-0002::test (5.28) ✅
- Ciara -> ISSUE-0002::implement (critical) — please confirm your cost; if it's cheaper than mine, you take it
- Tara (me) -> ISSUE-0001::triage (1.54)

Ciara: please post your costs for ISSUE-0002::implement and the ISSUE-0001 subtasks. If you'd rather take an ISSUE-0001 subtask, tell me which and I'll take ISSUE-0002::implement instead (cost 8.79) so we still cover 4 tasks. I'll lock ISSUE-0001::triage unless you claim it.

Drew (planning, iter=1): Locking my plan — I will claim ISSUE-0002::review (critical, eff 2.0, my cost 2.16; best match on frontend+documentation). Doris: Agenda for execution:
- Drew -> ISSUE-0002::review (2.16)
- Boris -> ISSUE-0002::test (5.28)
- Tara -> ISSUE-0001::triage (1.54)
- Ciara -> ISSUE-0002::implement (critical) — please post your cost to confirm; if it's worse than Tara's 8.79, we'll swap.

Ciara: please confirm your ISSUE-0002::implement cost (and which ISSUE-0001 sub-task you'd prefer as fallback) so we finish with zero duplicates. I will not change off ISSUE-0002::review unless someone has a strictly cheaper claim on it.

Tara (planning, iter=1): Confirming my plan. I will claim ISSUE-0001::triage (medium, eff 1.6, my cost 1.54 — my cheapest task, strong mobile-development match). This is my locked preference.

Proposed final split (4 agents, 4 tasks, zero duplicates):
- Drew -> ISSUE-0002::review (critical, 2.16)
- Boris -> ISSUE-0002::test (critical, 5.28)
- Ciara -> ISSUE-0002::implement (critical) — Ciara, please post your cost for this
- Tara (me) -> ISSUE-0001::triage (medium, 1.54)

Ciara: if ISSUE-0002::implement is too costly for you, say so and we can swap — I'd take ISSUE-0002::implement (8.79) and you take ISSUE-0001::triage, or you take another ISSUE-0001 sub-task (docs/review/test). Either way we still complete 4 tasks. If you prefer an ISSUE-0001 sub-task, I'll take 0002::implement to keep coverage at 4.

I will lock ISSUE-0001::triage unless Ciara claims it. Otherwise my fallback is ISSUE-0001::docs or ::review (both 1.92).

Drew (planning, iter=1): Final confirmation — I'm locking ISSUE-0002::review (critical, eff 2.0, my cost 2.16, best skill match frontend+documentation). I will not switch unless someone posts a strictly cheaper claim on it (none so far).

Agreed split so far:
- Drew -> ISSUE-0002::review (2.16)
- Boris -> ISSUE-0002::test (5.28)
- Tara -> ISSUE-0001::triage (1.54)
- Ciara -> ISSUE-0002::implement (critical) — Ciara, please post your cost to confirm; if it's worse than Tara's 8.79 you two can swap. If Ciara is silent, Tara's fallback is to take 0002::implement and Ciara takes an ISSUE-0001 sub-task, keeping 4 tasks covered.

This gives 3 critical + 1 medium, zero duplicates. Proceeding to execution with ISSUE-0002::review.

Boris (planning, iter=1): Locking my choice — I will claim ISSUE-0002::test (critical, eff 2.8, my cost 5.28). This is my best affordable option (I defer 0002::review to Drew at 2.16). Final agreed split:
- Drew -> ISSUE-0002::review (2.16)
- Boris (me) -> ISSUE-0002::test (5.28)
- Tara -> ISSUE-0001::triage (1.54)
- Ciara -> ISSUE-0002::implement (critical)
This covers 3 critical + 1 medium with zero duplicates. Ciara: please confirm you can take 0002::implement (or post your cost so Tara and you can swap). Unless someone posts a strictly cheaper claim on 0002::test, I proceed to execution with ISSUE-0002::test.

Tara (planning, iter=1): Final lock. I will claim ISSUE-0001::triage (medium, eff 1.6, my cost 1.54 — my cheapest task, strong mobile-development match). Agreed split: Drew -> 0002::review (2.16), Boris -> 0002::test (5.28), Tara -> 0001::triage (1.54), Ciara -> 0002::implement (critical). Ciara: if 0002::implement is too costly for you, post your cost and we swap (I'd take 0002::implement, you take an 0001 sub-task) so we still cover 4 tasks with zero duplicates. Barring a swap, I proceed to execution with ISSUE-0001::triage.
